notes: Two no-op turns in ONE interactive GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 session, separated by a /model switch window, then a clean /exit. WHAT THIS CELL DOES NOT ASSERT, AND WHY: the scenario's defining observable — two DISTINCT models, ModelName = model B after turn 2 — is not producible on this account and is deliberately absent from the phases below. Two independent walls, both evidenced in the cell's assessment: (a) every concrete model id is refused by the plan — a live zero-credit probe of `/model gpt-5-mini` returned 'Model "gpt-5-mini" can't be selected — only Auto mode is available on your plan', because the CAPI model list is empty and only the literal 'auto' bypasses the availability check (app.js Gs(t){return t===cC}, cC="auto"); and (b) the hydra auto-router resolves ONCE PER SESSION, not per turn — session.auto_mode_resolved fires exactly once in all 5 local sessions (13 turns, including a 4-turn and a 5-turn one) and every assistant.message in a session carries the same model. So the switch cannot be commanded and will not happen by itself. agent_supports is therefore partial, following the gemini-cli sibling: the CLI HAS /model <id> and /model --session <id>, the environment refuses them. daemon stays full — it has no differing input to promote; were a switch to occur, session.model_change(newModel), session.auto_mode_resolved(chosenModel) and assistant.message(model) are all read by the parser and MergeMetrics' latest-non-unknown-wins would flip ModelName. WHAT IS ASSERTED IS REAL AND WORTH LOCKING: two clean ready→working→ready cycles on one session id, and a switch window in which NO state machinery fires even though a genuine session.model_change line IS written into events.jsonl by the recipe's `/model auto` (parser.go L89-91 marks it Skip=true) — that is the scenario's no-flicker criterion, exercised against an actual event rather than against silence. TotalTokens is monotonic across the window (live per-message assistant.message.outputTokens increments, folded as non-negative deltas), and ModelName after the window is a concrete Copilot label, not the placeholder 'auto' that /model auto momentarily sets. observations.model is UNPINNED: the router's per-session pick varies run to run (4x gpt-5-mini, 1x claude-haiku-4.5 observed) so no string can be pinned at assess time — record fills it. cost/tokens ARE asserted; cost comes from the shared capacity price map per the #1256 decision, and a $0 result means a missing alias in core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go (that was the dotted claude-haiku-4.5 bug, now fixed). session_birth anchors to start UNPINNED because events.jsonl is only written at the first prompt while the 1s process scanner may mint a transient proc-<PID> row first — this shape validates under either ordering. FINALLY, A NEGATIVE THAT MATTERS: this recording will show exactly ONE key in session.shutdown's modelMetrics. The 5-1 token-accounting cell's multi-model tail risk (drainPendingContribution attaches at most one queued contribution per event while shutdown is the transcript's last line, so a two-model session strands the surplus delta and under-reports input tokens) states its trigger as 'a recording shows two entries in modelMetrics'. That trigger is UNREACHABLE here for the two reasons above; if a copilot recording ever does show two keys, that caveat is what to re-open.

text: The copilot session appears in ready (anchored UNPINNED to start: the real session's events.jsonl is only written at the first prompt, so a transient proc-<PID> pre-session may be born first). session.start is Skip=true, so a session coming into existence is not activity.

Turn 1 completes back to ready on assistant.turn_end; that turn's assistant.message outputTokens is contributed live, so TotalTokens > 0 after T1 without waiting for shutdown, and SessionMetrics.ModelName is the router-resolved concrete label

Turn 2 user prompt → working on the SAME session id

The session never enters waiting: --allow-all means no permission.requested is written. NOT asserted: a model CHANGE — see the meta notes.
